fields.Name: Advocacy Updates from the International Cheese Federation
fields.Description: This page from the International Cheese Federation's website features recent blog posts categorized under 'Advocacy.' The posts address critical issues impacting the cheese industry, including backlogs in routine facility inspections, delays in federal agriculture data releases, challenges with cheese oversupply and declining exports, stagnant farmgate milk prices, and regulatory hurdles concerning raw milk, aged curds, and interstate distribution limits. The articles highlight the Federation's active role in advocating on behalf of its members to policymakers and relevant committees.

The inspection backlog, and what we’re asking on your behalf 

 

Routine facility inspections paused for over a month this winter and are only now catching up. Here’s what that backlog means for members and what our Food Safety Committee is pushing for. 


Continue Reading

The numbers came back all at once 

 

Six weeks of missing federal agriculture data landed in a single release this morning. Here is what the federation is asking for on behalf of members who plan a year at a time.

The cheese nobody can move 

 

Cold-storage warehouses are holding more cheese than they ever have, exports are down, and farmgate milk prices are stuck. Here is what the federation is asking policymakers to do about it.

Raw milk, aged curds, and the line at the state border 

 

As state legislative sessions convene across the country, new bills on farmstead dairy sales are landing on committee dockets while artisan cheesemakers navigate federal sixty-day aging rules and interstate distribution limits.
